question: does any effort= threshold separate codex from claude in the USEFUL direction (codex -> thinking models, claude not)?
semantics: effort=<level> is AT LEAST that level: the rule renders as 'effort >= high', and a medium request misses it (rule n 0) while a high request hits it (rule n 1). Proven on scratch group hp-eff, since removed.

thresholds.effort=high: matches CLAUDE only - the wrong one

answer: NO. At Cookrew's defaults claude asks high and codex asks medium, so the ordering is inverted: a >= predicate can never select the lower level and exclude the higher. No effort= threshold does what the route program wanted.
options: a bearer per harness (magpie-claude / magpie-codex): agents= then matches, because agentOf() takes the agent from the token first. Costs the single cookrew Usage identity.

invert the rule instead of the traffic: make the group's ORDER put the thinking model first (codex's medium matches nothing and lands there) and add effort=high -> <chat model> so claude's high effort is the thing the rule moves. Needs no new bearer and no spoofed effort.

manufacture the gap: route-env adds -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh for codex cards so effort=xhigh matches codex alone. Overrides the card's EFF dial and sets a reasoning level for a reason that is not about reasoning.
